privacy.title: Privacy / Data Retention
privacy.explanation: This page controls the cleanup of old messaging, conversation state, and operational records according to the retention policy. Patient, appointment, treatment, payment, and legal audit records are not deleted by this process.

autoCleanup.title: Automatic Cleanup Control
autoCleanup.envDisabledWarning: Automatic cleanup is disabled at the environment level (DATA_RETENTION_CLEANUP_ENABLED=false). It cannot be enabled from the UI.
autoCleanup.runtimeDisabledWarning: Automatic cleanup is disabled via the UI setting. Use the toggle above to enable it.

legacyConsentCorrection.title: Legacy Consent Correction Workflow (Kill Switch)
legacyConsentCorrection.explanation: This is a platform-wide kill switch for the KVKK-HIGH-008 legacy SMS opt-out correction workflow — not a pilot-clinic allowlist. While off, no clinic can create a new correction record; existing correction history always remains viewable.

privacy.liveRunBlockedEnvDisabled: Live cleanup cannot run because it is disabled at the system level (DATA_RETENTION_CLEANUP_ENABLED=false).
privacy.actionsNote: Dry-run shows the number of records that would be affected without deleting any data.
privacy.runFailed: Cleanup could not be run. Please try again.
privacy.unauthorizedError: You are not authorized to perform this action.
privacy.confirmWarning: This will permanently delete or anonymize old communication data. Make sure you have run a dry-run first.

backups.title: Database Backups
backups.actionsNote: Use the buttons below to trigger a manual backup or run a restore test. The production database is never touched.
backups.alreadyRunning: An operation is already running, please wait
backups.noBackupAlarmDetail: There is not a single database backup file. A failure right now would lose all patient data permanently. Run a backup immediately and fix the schedule.
backups.dbStaleDetail: The most recent database backup was taken {{age}}, beyond the {{hours}} h threshold. The scheduled backup is probably not running.
backups.recoveryUnavailableDetail: The consolidated recovery status could not be loaded, so file backup and restore drill information is not shown. Only the database backup tier below is current.
backups.fileTotalsFailuresNote: The ledger holds files that were never copied or verified. Those files have no second copy.
backups.fileDisabledDetail: Patient attachments and imaging have no second copy at all. Losing the primary storage loses them permanently. Enable file backup.
backups.fileNoDestinationDetail: File backup is enabled but has nowhere to write. No attachment or imaging file is being copied.
backups.fileOnHostTitle: FILE BACKUP DESTINATION IS ON THE SAME HOST
backups.fileOnHostDetail: The copy lives on the production host, so a host loss destroys the original and the backup together. This is not an independent backup.
backups.fileFailuresDetail: The last run reported {{failed}} failed file(s) and {{missing}} file(s) missing at source. Those files are not protected.
backups.fileStaleDetail: The last file backup run was {{age}}, beyond the {{hours}} h threshold.
backups.drillsNote: Duration is the measured recovery time (RTO). Source artifact age is the measured effective data loss window (RPO).
backups.drillNeverRunDetail: Recovery has never been proven. An untested backup is not a backup.
backups.drillStaleWarning: No drill within the last {{hours}} h
backups.residualTitle: RESIDUAL RESTORE ARTIFACT LEFT ON PRODUCTION
backups.residualDetail: A restore drill failed to clean up after itself. A full plaintext copy of the patient database is still present on the production cluster. Drop each object listed below immediately.
backups.pitrNote: Continuous WAL archiving to an encrypted pgBackRest repository. Reported by a separate host-side writer; the application never runs pgBackRest itself.
backups.pitrNotConfiguredHint: PITR is not active. Enabling continuous WAL archiving requires an approved freeze exception and a PostgreSQL restart — see the F4 recovery operations runbook. Until then, recovery resolution is limited to the daily 03:15 pg_dump.

pitrReason.clock_skew: Status file timestamp is in the future

backups.pitrCommandBrokenTitle: WAL archiving is on but the archive_command has been altered
backups.pitrCommandBrokenDetail: PostgreSQL is marking WAL segments as archived and recycling them, but they are not reaching the repository. Backups will keep succeeding while the recovery chain has a permanent hole. Restore the exact archive_command and verify with pgbackrest check.
backups.pitrPlaintextTitle: The pgBackRest repository is not encrypted
backups.pitrPlaintextDetail: The repository holds a physical copy of every table, including special-category health data, and no patient column is encrypted at column level. Repository encryption is the only confidentiality control on this artifact.
backups.pitrInactiveTitle: pgBackRest is installed but WAL archiving is off
backups.pitrInactiveDetail: The repository exists but archive_mode is not on, so there is no point-in-time recovery capability and worst-case data loss remains bounded only by the daily backup interval.
backups.pitrWalStaleTitle: WAL archiving has stalled — the recoverable point is falling behind
backups.pitrWalStaleDetail: The newest archived WAL segment is {{age}} old (threshold {{minutes}} minutes). Backups and archive_command still report success, so nothing else on this page turns red — but every transaction since then is unrecoverable. Check `pgbackrest check` and the PostgreSQL log for archive_command failures.
